Unit One
Parts of Speech
Lesson 1: Nouns
A. Look at the underlined words in the following passage:

subject: English_grammar
text:
Anika is in class seven. She lives in a village of Jamalpur with her parents.
She has two sisters. She often takes them to school. She has to help her
mother as well. Her father is a small businessman. In her free time, Anika
likes to draw pictures and write poems in Bangla. Anika’s dream is to
become a computer engineer.

subject: English_grammar
text:
These are all nouns. A noun is a word used to refer to people, animals,
objects, substances, states, events, ideas and feelings.
B. Nouns can be countable or uncountable. The nouns which can be counted
are countable and those which cannot be counted are uncountable.
Read the following sentences and say whether the underlined nouns are
countable or uncountable:

subject: English_grammar
text:
He has many friends.
Kamal has given me some good news.
Urmi borrowed some books from the library.
Afsana eats bread for breakfast.
Zahid's father is a teacher.
C. Countable nouns have two forms: singular and plural. The singular form
refers to one person or thing and the plural form refers to more than one
person or thing.
Forma-1, English Grammar and Composition, 7

subject: English_grammar

2 English Grammar and Composition
a. How to make plurals
Regular plurals are formed by adding 's' to the singular forms of nouns.
For example:
book------------- books
flower---------------- flowers
teacher---------- teachers
watch-------------- watches
class---------------- classes
box---------------- boxes
c. Nouns ending in consonants and ‘y’ change to ‘ies’ in the plurals.For
example:

subject: English_grammar
text:
country -------------- countries
victory -------------- victories
lady ---------------------- ladies
boy --------------- boys
day -------------------- days
key -------------- keys

Lesson 2: Pronouns
A. Look at the underlined words in the following texts :
a. Mr Ahmed is reading a book. It is very interesting.
b. Students of this school are very disciplined. They all stay in the hostel.

subject: English_grammar
text:
c. The game teacher asked players to go to the field in the afternoon. But
nobody was there.

subject: English_grammar
text:
Note: Here 'It' refers to a book, ' they' refers to students and ‘nobody’ refers
to players. Here it, they and nobody are called pronouns as they are used
instead of nouns. In other words, pronouns are alternatives to nouns. When
something or someone is already mentioned in a sentence you refer to them
again by using a pronoun.

These are all adverbs. Can you guess what words they modify?

Note : ‘Personally’gives the speaker’s attitude. We often use comma (,) after

subject: English_grammar
text:
An adverb comes after a verb. It is usually a word but sometimes a group of
words modifies a verb. Then that group is called an adverbial phrase. Any
adverb or adverbial phrase that modifies a verb is called an adverbial.
Rakib looked at his friends nervously after he had lost his admit cards.
Here the underlined word describes how something has happened. This is an
adverbial of manner.

subject: English_grammar
text:
The toy was lying on the table.
Here the item describes where something was. It is an adverbial of place.
They visited their hometown last month.
Here the underlined item tells when something happens. It is an adverbial of
time.

Lesson 7: Conjunctions and Interjections
A. Read the following passage and notice the words in bold:
Dipu and Raj are good friends but they are not of the same age. They have

subject: English_grammar
text:
been even together as neighbours. Many years back they thought they would
settle abroad but after their higher study overseas they decided to buy land in
the same area. When they found it together, Raj said to Dipu, "Let’s buy it now
or never".
The words and, but, or, because, yet are called conjunctions. The main
function of these words is to link words, phrases and clauses together.

subject: English_grammar
text:
Now write five sentences using each of the above conjunctions.
B. Read the following sentences and notice the underlined words:
Wow, so big a cake!
Alas! They have lost the game.
Oops, | have got hurt!
Omg, how could you do that!
The above underlined words are interjections. An interjection is a part of
speech which expresses a strong feeling of joy, pain, surprise or disgust.
